question: Which Five Year Plan marked the beginning of the Green Revolution in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Five Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Third Five Year Plan (1961-1966) marked the beginning of the Green Revolution in India.
 
• It focused on increasing agricultural production through the adoption of modern farming techniques.
 
• The introduction of High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, better irrigation facilities, and chemical fertilizers were key elements of the Green Revolution during this period.
 
• The Green Revolution aimed to achieve self-sufficiency in food grain production, particularly wheat and rice.
 
• Norman Borlaug's research on dwarf wheat varieties greatly influenced India's Green Revolution efforts, starting with pilot projects in states like Punjab and Haryana.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five Year Plans in India**

 
 
• India adopted planned development through Five Year Plans starting in 1951.
 
• These plans aimed at balanced economic growth across various sectors such as agriculture, industry, and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution**
 
 
• It was a set of initiatives aimed at enhancing agricultural productivity using modern methods.
 
• The Green Revolution in India was spearheaded by M.S. Swaminathan, known as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India."
 
• It was instrumental in reducing India's dependence on food imports during the 1960s.
 
 
 
• **Key Technologies of Green Revolution**
 
 
• High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and modern irrigation techniques were introduced.
 
• Mechanization of agriculture, including tractors and other farming equipment, also played a significant role.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Green Revolution**
 
 
• It led to a substantial increase in food grain production, particularly wheat and rice.
 
• States like Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh became agricultural hubs due to the Green Revolution.
 
• While it enhanced food security, it also brought challenges such as environmental degradation and regional disparities.
